narrative: Three well-educated Syrian Kurds from Qamishli, near the Turkish border, who could not pursue their studies or find decent work in Syria or Iraqi Kurdistan, set out for Europe hoping for a future in Germany. They were promised transport by a smuggler. In August 2015 they were packed into a refrigerated truck in Hungary bound for Germany via Austria, alongside dozens of other people - 71 in all, including eight women and four children, from Syria, Iraq and Afghanistan. The refrigeration was not running and there was no ventilation; packed roughly five to a square meter, the people inside realized they were suffocating and banged on the walls and screamed for the driver to stop. The traffickers, coordinating by phone, refused to open the doors and instead abandoned the locked truck on a highway near the town of Parndorf, just inside Austria. Within about two hours of the traffickers leaving, everyone inside had suffocated. The bodies were found on 27 August 2015; the men were among the 59 men, eight women and four children who died. Four traffickers were later jailed for life over the deaths.
